belief: I must suffer in purgatory before I can be with God.
meta: A Christian look at the fear that you must suffer in purgatory before you can be with God, with Scripture, questions, and homework for resting in the truth.
origins: Teaching about purgatory from childhood. Fear of suffering after death for sins you have not fully made up for. Pictures of punishment that made death frightening. Grief and worry about loved ones who have died. Christian traditions differ on this teaching; this card focuses on the fear that Christ’s work is not enough to bring you to God.
teaches: Scripture points believers to the complete sufficiency of Christ. By a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified. After He provided purification for sins, He sat down, because the work was finished. To the thief on the cross, Jesus promised, “Today you will be with Me in Paradise.” Paul expected that to be away from the body is to be at home with the Lord. You can face death with hope, trusting what Christ has done.
self_statements: I’ll have to suffer a long time before I see God.
My sins aren’t fully paid for yet.
I’m terrified of what happens after I die.
I have to suffer more now to shorten it later.
My loved one is suffering because of me.
Christ’s death covered some of my sins, but not all.
errors: Picturing the worst possible suffering after death.
Believing His sacrifice was not enough.
Letting fear of the future rob your present peace.
Concluding “I feel unworthy, so I must be punished.”
questions: What did Jesus promise the thief on the cross, who had no time to make up for anything?
What does Hebrews 10:14 say Christ’s one offering accomplished?
Why did Jesus sit down after purifying sins?
Is there any condemnation for those in Christ Jesus?
Where did Paul expect to be when he died?
Am I trusting Christ’s work, or adding my own?
What would change if I faced death with hope?
truth: I do not have to fear suffering after death to pay for my sins. Christ’s one offering has made me perfect forever in God’s sight. There is no condemnation for me in Christ Jesus. When I die, I will be at home with the Lord. I can face death with hope because Jesus finished the work.
hw_questions: What did Jesus promise the thief on the cross?
What did Christ’s one offering accomplish?
Is there condemnation for me in Christ?
Where did Paul expect to be after death?
Am I trusting Christ’s work or adding my own?
hw_truths: Christ’s one offering has made me perfect forever.
There is no condemnation for me in Christ Jesus.
To be away from the body is to be at home with the Lord.
Jesus finished the work of purifying my sins.
I can face death with hope.
My salvation rests on Christ, not on my suffering.
log: Each day, write one thing I look forward to about being with the Lord.

“Jesus, my hope is in You,” and read Romans 8:1.
tracker: One thing I look forward to
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You finished the work of purifying my sins. Help me reject the fear that I must suffer before I can be with You. Thank You that there is no condemnation for me in You, and that to be away from the body is to be at home with You. Give me hope as I think about the future. In Your name, Amen.
